transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Well, nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. My family actually brought me in. 

See, we were down at the fair, and I was giving a talk. But... well, I ended up climbing right up onto the tractor in the middle of it. I kept jerking the controls around because I needed to show the crowd the... the 'new pattern'. And I just couldn't make myself stop doing it, even with people yelling at me to get down. So, they decided I needed to come see you.
Before this episode at the fair, had you used any alcohol, drugs, or new medications in the days leading up to it?
No, I haven't. I don't really drink, and I definitely don't mess with any drugs. As far as medications go... well, I haven't started anything new at all. Just my usual routine leading up to it.

During this time at the fair, did you experience anything like hearing voices others couldn't hear, or holding beliefs—like about the 'new pattern' having special significance—that others told you weren't true?

Well, yes, I do hear voices. It wasn't just at the fair, though. Mostly it happens out by the north pasture, especially right around dusk. 

I hear these clear voices coming right out of the irrigation lines. They tell me exactly which rows of the crops are poisoned, and which ones are blessed. And... well, the thing is, it's not just when I'm all fired up and energetic like I was on that tractor. It still happens on regular weeks, too, when I'm not feeling wound up at all.

During those times when you hear the voices from the irrigation lines but aren't feeling wound up or energetic, is your mood completely normal, or do you notice feeling depressed, low, or lacking energy during those periods?

Well, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or low, no. My mood is just... regular, I guess. 

There were several quieter weeks where I wasn't feeling especially energized or, you know, grand like I was on that tractor. Just normal. But even during those quiet weeks, I still heard the lines talking to me out there. And I still firmly believed that the farm data was carrying hidden warnings. So, I wasn't wound up at all, but I was still hearing and seeing all those things.
Overall, how long has this been going on in total — from when you first started hearing the voices and noticing these energized episodes, up to now?

Well, if I look back on the whole thing... it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right around the time we refinanced the property and began that big farm readjustment. That's when I first started noticing the voices and having those spells where I couldn't stop working.

Over this past year and two months, roughly how much of that time would you say you were in one of those energized, 'can't stop' episodes like on the tractor, compared to the quieter weeks where your mood was normal?

Well, if I add it all up... I'd say the majority of the time I've been in that wound-up state. Those charged, sleepless, nonstop stretches where I'm just going and going... that's probably taken up about ten months out of the last year and two months. The quieter, regular weeks just kind of happen in between those long stretches.

Critically, these hallucinations and delusions persisted during clearly delineated periods of euthymic, non-manic mood ('regular weeks') lasting at least 2 months, confirming psychotic symptoms occur independent of mood episodes—ruling out mood disorder with psychotic features (F30.2). Mood episode symptoms (manic) have been present for the majority of the total illness duration (~10 of 14 months), satisfying the requirement that mood symptoms be present for a substantial portion of the illness, which distinguishes this from primary Schizophrenia (F20.9). No substance use or medical explanation was identified. The combination of mood episode plus concurrent psychosis, psychosis without mood symptoms for a distinct period, and mood symptoms predominating over the illness course supports Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type.
